summary: Hajime Sakurabe was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Otani University, studying under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, and later held posts there (1949–1986), Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1956–1958), and Doho University (~1996–2000).

Hajime Tanabe worked in philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and later under Kitaro Nishida, Heinrich Rickert, and Martin Heidegger. His main academic posts were at Tohoku University (1913) and Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711). He also taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, and abroad at Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Komazawa, and Nagoya universities.

Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Toshima Normal School and under teachers including Bokusan Nishiari and Sogaku Daiun Harada. He founded Sanbo Zen in 1954 and taught numerous students.
Halle Elizabeth O'Neal is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Kansas under doctoral supervisor Sherry Fowler (attested 2011).

Hammalawa Saddhatissa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He held posts at Maha Bodhi College, Banaras Hindu University, SOAS, the University of Toronto, and headed the London Buddhist Vihara (1957–1990).
Hank Glassman is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held faculty posts at Haverford College (attested 2009 and 2019).

Hanns Oertel specialized in Indology and linguistics, earning his doctorate at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale (1891–1917), Harvard (1903–1904), Marburg (1922), and Munich (1925–1935).

Hanns-Peter Schmidt was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf. He held academic posts at Deccan College, Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, Tübingen, and UCLA (1965–2000).
Hannu K. Riikonen studied at the University of Helsinki from 1967 to 1978. He later served there as a professor from approximately 1999 to 2014.

Hans Delbrück was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873). He held academic posts at Frederick William University Berlin (1885) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1885–1921).

Hans Harder is an Indology scholar who completed his Magister at Heidelberg University and his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das and Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where he served as Assistent (1995–2007).

Hans Hartog was an Indology scholar who studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Bethel, Munich, and Marburg, where he completed his PhD under Friedrich Heiler. He was also taught by Hanns Oertel, Walther Wüst, and others.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held academic appointments at Leipzig University (~1930–1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1931–1946), and the University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who completed graduate studies at Northwestern and Yale, studying under Warren Cowgill. He served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1967, ~1982–2013).
Hans Krahe was a linguist who held academic posts at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1946), Heidelberg University (~1947–1949), and the University of Tübingen (~1949–1965).

Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University, Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum (~1948–1955), and the Catholic University of Paris (~1955–1956), and later served on the faculty at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).

Hans T. Bakker is an Indologist who studied under Jacob Ensink. He held a post at the University of Groningen (~1981–2013), was a visiting fellow at All Souls College, Oxford, and served as curator at the British Museum.
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar who held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1935).
